chunk_findings.detail: The default `bandit_command` is `bandit -q -ll`, which tells Bandit to report only medium-severity-and-above issues. The acceptance scenario explicitly requires that a changed file containing a B608 pattern fails smoke, but B608 (`hardcoded_sql_expressions`) is a low-severity Bandit finding. With the default knob value, a changed file such as one containing `cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '%s'" % name)` produces a B608 finding that is filtered out by `-ll`, so Bandit exits 0 and the smoke gate records the Bandit check as passed instead of failed. This defeats the stated purpose of catching the B608 regression.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/smoke.py:42

chunk_findings.detail: The test named for the acceptance criterion “the probe list equals the registry list” does not actually enforce equality for most registries. It only checks exact equality for `ddflow.surfaces.declared.*` against `family_modules()`, then uses `registered <= sections` for config sections, and for `core.handlers` and `surfaces.tools` it only asserts that at least one module was found and is importable. For example, if `S.probe_modules(ROOT)` also returned a non-registered module such as `ddflow.surfaces.tools.junk` or `ddflow.config_sections._docs`, or omitted some registered tool/event modules while still returning at least one matching prefix, these assertions would still pass. That lets the implementation probe a hand-kept or overbroad module list while the test appears to prove registry equality.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_smoke_gate.py:test_the_probe_list_equals_the_registry_list

chunk_findings.detail: The final assertion calls `S.changed_files(root, "main")` only after `S.run_configured(root, "main", cfg)` has already run the default ruff check. Ruff normally creates `.ruff_cache` in the project directory it checks, which here is the temporary git root. Since the test itself requires `changed_files` to include the untracked file `ddflow/bad.py`, any `changed_files` implementation that includes untracked files (e.g. via `git status --porcelain`) will also see the newly created cache directory unless it has a special cache filter, making the equality `["ddflow/bad.py"]` fail. If instead `changed_files` excludes untracked files, the preceding ruff assertion fails because ruff would have no changed file to check. The test should query `changed_files` before mutating the tree, or otherwise isolate/disable tool caches.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_smoke_gate.py:test_run_configured_reads_every_knob_from_the_config_and_names_the_changed_files

chunk_findings.detail: `--diff-filter=d` selects *only deleted* files; git's `--diff-filter` includes the statuses spelled in lowercase and excludes them only when uppercase (`--diff-filter=M` = modified only, `--diff-filter=D` = everything but deleted). So the "committed, staged, modified" half of the documented set is never collected: given a merge where the branch has committed `ddflow/surfaces/declared/dispatch.py` containing an f-string SQL query (the B608 pattern named in the decision) and a changed test, `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=d origin/main` returns nothing (no deletions), and the only paths that survive are whatever `git ls-files --others` reports; the deleted names that do come back are then dropped by `_py`'s `(root / c).is_file()` test. Net effect: `files == []`, so `_ruff` and `_bandit` return `SKIPPED`, `_tests` returns `SKIPPED`, the probe passes, and `Report.outcome` is `passed` — the gate green-lights exactly the committed B608/failing-test change it was built to catch, and acceptance criterion "a fixture with a B608 pattern fails smoke" only holds if the fixture happens to be untracked.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/smoke.py:287 (`changed_files`)

chunk_findings.detail: When `root` does not contain `_DECLARED`/`_REGISTERING_DIRS` (root handed in as a subdirectory, a shallow/partial checkout, or a tree with a different layout), `probe_modules` returns `[]`, `_run` invokes the probe script with no module arguments, the script prints `{}`, and `_probe` returns `Check("probe", PASSED, "0 modules")`. The one check whose entire job is to prove that every registering module imports reports `passed` having imported nothing, so the overall report can be `passed` while the probe verified zero modules; a check that verified nothing should be `skipped`/`unavailable`, never `passed`, per the decision's "never passed" rule for checks that did not actually run.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/smoke.py:150 (`_probe`) / `probe_modules`

chunk_findings.detail: The default `bandit -q -ll` filters out low-confidence Bandit findings, and B608 (`hardcoded_sql_expressions`) is a low-confidence finding. Given a changed file containing the B608 pattern that previously broke `main`, smoke runs `bandit -q -ll <file>`, Bandit suppresses the B608 report and exits 0, so the gate records bandit as passed and allows the merge. This directly violates the acceptance case “a fixture with a B608 pattern fails smoke” and the stated reason for the gate.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.smoke.bandit_command.toml:4

chunk_findings.detail: `test_a_missing_bandit_is_unavailable_and_the_other_checks_still_run` passes `ruff_command=str(ROOT / ".venv/bin/ruff")` and then asserts at line 86 that the `ruff` check is `PASSED`. In any valid environment where the repo virtualenv is not at `ROOT/.venv` — for example, a Windows checkout where the binary is under `.venv/Scripts/ruff.exe`, a CI image where `ruff` is installed elsewhere or provided via `uv run`, or a source checkout with no `.venv` directory — that path does not exist. Smoke should correctly record `ruff` as `UNAVAILABLE`, but the test fails because it expected `PASSED`. The same hidden dependency appears at line 136/139, where `.venv/bin/python` is hardcoded and the test expects the `tests` check to be `FAILED`; if that path is missing, the check becomes `UNAVAILABLE` and the test fails for an environment reason unrelated to the smoke gate.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_smoke_gate.py:82

chunk_findings.detail: The test named `test_the_probe_list_equals_the_registry_list` does not actually enforce equality for most registries. For config sections it only asserts `registered <= sections`, so extra probed modules such as `ddflow.config_sections._docs` pass even though they are not registry-derived. For handlers/tools/events it only asserts that each package prefix has some probed module and that those modules import; it never compares that set to the registry-derived set. For example, if `S.probe_modules(ROOT)` omitted `ddflow.core.handlers.event_kind` but still returned another module under `ddflow.core.handlers.`, line 166 would pass, or if it included unrelated `ddflow.config_sections.*` modules, line 163 would pass. That allows the acceptance criterion “probe list equals the registry list” to be false while this test still passes.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_smoke_gate.py:163

chunk_findings.detail: The default `bandit_command` is `bandit -q -ll`. In Bandit, `-ll` raises the reporting threshold to HIGH severity only, while `B608` (`hardcoded_sql_expressions`) is reported at MEDIUM severity. Given a changed Python file containing a B608 pattern such as `sql = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = %s" % user_id`, the default smoke gate runs Bandit with `-ll`, Bandit exits with no reported findings, the bandit check is recorded as passed, and the merge is not refused. This defeats the stated acceptance requirement that a fixture containing a B608 pattern must fail smoke.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/smoke.py:43

chunk_findings.detail: The default bandit command is `bandit -q -ll`, and Bandit’s `-ll` restricts output to high-severity issues only. The accepted acceptance criteria explicitly require a fixture containing a B608 hardcoded-SQL pattern to fail the smoke gate, but B608 is not a high-severity Bandit finding by default; with `-ll` it is filtered out, so Bandit exits 0 and the smoke check records bandit as passed rather than failed. A command such as `bandit -q -l` (or no severity filter, letting project config decide) is needed to catch the known B608 regression.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.smoke.bandit_command.toml:4

chunk_findings.detail: The test named for the acceptance criterion “the probe list equals the registry list” does not actually enforce that equality for tools, commands, or event kinds. It only requires exact equality for `ddflow.surfaces.declared` family modules, a subset relation for config-section modules, and that at least one importable module exists under `ddflow.core.handlers` and `ddflow.surfaces.tools`. If `probe_modules(ROOT)` were changed to omit all command/event/tool registry modules except one arbitrary importable module in each of those two packages, the assertions would still pass: the declared-family set could match, `registered <= sections` could hold, and the `found` sets would be non-empty. Thus a regression where the smoke gate stops probing command or event modules is not caught.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_smoke_gate.py:test_the_probe_list_equals_the_registry_list

chunk_findings.detail: Several tests hard-code repository virtual-environment executables such as `ROOT/.venv/bin/ruff` and `ROOT/.venv/bin/python`. For example, `test_ruff_finding_fails` passes `ruff_command=str(ROOT / ".venv/bin/ruff")`; on Windows the venv executable path is `.venv/Scripts/ruff.exe`, and in any environment where ruff is available elsewhere but not at that exact path, `S.run` records `UNAVAILABLE`, so the assertion `outcome == FAILED` fails. The test result therefore depends on the exact virtualenv layout rather than on whether the smoke gate correctly fails a ruff finding.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_smoke_gate.py:test_ruff_finding_fails

chunk_findings.detail: The new tracked-files command still only compares the working tree to `base`; it never compares the index to `base`, despite the docstring promising “staged” changes. Given a clean repo at `main` with a safe `q.py`, stage a B608 version of `q.py` (`git add q.py`) and then edit the working tree back to the safe content. `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=d main` sees the working tree as unchanged from `main` and returns nothing, and `git ls-files --others` also returns nothing, so `changed_files` returns `[]`. Smoke then skips ruff/bandit on `q.py` and can report `passed` even though the staged blob that would be committed contains the B608 pattern.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/smoke.py:274 (`changed_files`)

chunk_findings.detail: The new assertion still does not enforce that the probe list is registry-derived; it only enforces that every on-disk top-level module in `ddflow.config_sections` is probed. If `ddflow/config_sections/_docs.py` exists but does not register a config section, and `probe_modules` returns `ddflow.config_sections._docs` (for example because it scans the directory rather than the registry), then `registered <= sections` is true and `sections == on_disk` is also true, so the test passes even though the probe list contains a module that is not in `SECTION_CLASSES`. This leaves the acceptance case “probe list equals the registry list” untested for extra on-disk, non-registered modules.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_smoke_gate.py:167 (`test_the_probe_list_equals_the_registry_list`)

chunk_findings.detail: The new command string `f"{sys.executable} -m ruff"` (and similarly `test_command=f"{sys.executable} -m pytest ..."` at line 138) embeds `sys.executable` unquoted. In a valid environment where the interpreter path contains spaces, such as Windows `C:\Program Files\Python312\python.exe` or a virtualenv under a path with spaces, the command is split or shell-parsed into multiple argv tokens/words instead of one executable path. Smoke then cannot run the intended ruff/pytest interpreter, records the check as unavailable/failed, and the test fails while asserting `checks["ruff"].outcome == S.PASSED`.
